narrative.overview:
GoMail is designed as a luminous coastal reading room for everyday desktop correspondence. Rather than mimicking crowded browser webmail or fracturing into competing application skins, the entire desktop shell—titlebar, collapsible account rail, message ledger, long-form reading sheet, composer, settings tabs, and guarded upcoming views—shares one disciplined architectural system. Three stepped tonal planes step smoothly toward the reading surface, letting the user's eye settle effortlessly on the message at hand while preserving instant scannability across accounts, unread counts, and sync state.

Built as a local-first Go and MyGO WebView desktop client operating across macOS, Linux, and Windows, the visual language pairs unhurried clarity with honest operational feedback. Marine Cerulean marks intentional focus and primary action, while warm Terracotta is held exclusively for high-trust operational signals—blocked trackers and remote images, offline pauses, failed or queued remote writes, and uncertain send outcomes. Everything ships locally with zero network CDN dependencies, pairing OS-native humanist sans-serifs for seamless Chinese (`zh`) and English (`en`) prose across both daylit Harbor and Deep-Harbor dark modes, while leaving independent message-detail reading templates untouched.

Confirmed visual rejections shape this restraint: GoMail rejects generic grey-blue SaaS inbox chrome, rejects the legacy five-theme application switcher in favor of one unified Harbor system (`harbor`) with independent `light` / `dark` / `system` modes, rejects thick colored side-stripes on rows or callouts, rejects uppercase eyebrow kickers above view headings, and rejects decorative entrance staggers in favor of brisk, purposeful state feedback.
keyCharacteristics: Three-step tonal depth stepping cleanly from Harbor Mist chrome (`#ebf1f4` / `#0e1721`) through Chalk Sea lists (`#f7fafb` / `#131e2a`) to a crisp Reading Sheet (`#ffffff` / `#172432`).
Strict 56px shared horizontal baseline aligning pane headers, message action toolbars, compose bars, and secondary mail headings across the workspace.
Active focus isolation on mail and thread rows using a washed cerulean fill and a `1px` inset hairline border rather than heavy shadows or left stripes.
Reserved Terracotta signal beacons uniting privacy blocking, offline notices, outbox warnings, and failed remote writes into one unmistakable channel.

Local-only OS typography calibrated for bilingual Chinese and English reading (`15px` / `1.82` leading inside a `740px` reading sheet) with `tabular-nums` alignment across every ledger count and timestamp.
Independent 9-template message-detail reading architecture (`app` default plus 8 adaptive and fixed-palette skins) decoupled from the unified application shell.

rules.name: The Three-Plane Luminance Rule
rules.body: Chrome (`#ebf1f4` / `#0e1721`), triage lists (`#f7fafb` / `#131e2a`), and the reading sheet (`#ffffff` / `#172432`) step progressively brighter in both light and dark modes so reading always owns visual focus without decorative borders.

rules.name: The Terracotta Signal Doctrine
rules.body: Warm Terracotta (`#b84a24` / `#ee936e` on `#fdf4ee` / `#2a1d19`) is reserved exclusively for privacy protection, offline status, queued/failed remote writes, and uncertain send outcomes; never spend it on promotional accents, unread badges, or routine navigation.

rules.name: The Marine Focus Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Marine Cerulean (`#155e8a` / `#62b3e3`) marks active selection, unread pips, primary CTAs, and keyboard focus rings only—never paint entire chrome regions or passive containers in the primary accent.

rules.name: The Bilingual Legibility Rule
rules.body: Never apply `text-transform: uppercase` to navigation section headings or bilingual UI labels; preserve natural casing, maintain `1.82` reading line-height for dense Chinese and English paragraphs, and truncate CJK sender monograms to a single glyph (vs. up to two Latin initials).

rules.name: The Tabular Ledger Rule
rules.body: Apply `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` to every unread count pill, message timestamp, thread date, statusbar readout, and shortcut cap so numbers stay vertically locked during live sync updates.

rules.name: The 56px Shared Horizon Rule
rules.body: Every primary pane header—Inbox list header, native Reader action toolbar, Thread reader header, Compose header, Starred header, and Search toolbar—holds a `56px` minimum height with a `1px` bottom hairline so adjacent panes share one continuous horizontal datum line.

rules.name: The Single-Slot Ledger Rule
rules.body: Reserve a fixed `30px` trailing slot (`24px` below `760px`) for unread counts on every sidebar row and align nested folder labels to the parent account's trailing edge so counts form one vertical column and never shift labels when mail arrives.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Flatness Rule
rules.body: Keep navigation panes, list rows, reading sheets, and form fieldsets flat at rest; spend elevation shadows exclusively on primary triggers, expanded thread disclosures, floating menus, toasts, and modal overlays.

rules.name: The Crisp State-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Limit motion to direct 150ms–190ms state responses (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`); suppress transitions during theme switches and zero them completely under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

dos: Do step surfaces cleanly across the three luminance planes—Harbor Mist chrome (`#ebf1f4` / `#0e1721`), Chalk Sea lists (`#f7fafb` / `#131e2a`), and Reading Sheet (`#ffffff` / `#172432`)—for every view including Settings and guarded views.
Do align every primary pane header, reader toolbar, compose bar, and secondary mail heading to the `56px` shared horizontal baseline (`--ui-pane-header-height`).
Do reserve Terracotta signal tokens (`--color-signal*`) strictly for privacy blocking, offline state, queued/failed remote writes, and uncertain send outcomes.
Do set `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on every count badge, date, timestamp, shortcut badge, and status bar readout.

Do use the local OS font stack (`--font-ui`, `--font-mono`, `--font-serif`) with `1.82` reading line-height inside a `740px` measure so bilingual Chinese and English mail renders comfortably offline with zero CDN requests.

Do preserve keyboard `:focus-visible` outlines (`2px solid var(--color-accent)`), roving ARIA tablists, live status regions, `html[data-theme-switching]` zero-flash switching, and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` overrides on all interactive controls.
Do keep message-detail reading templates (`--msg-*` / `data-msg-*`) decoupled from application chrome tokens and preserve the dark-mode light-sheet link contrast guard (`#155e8a`).

Do render guarded/upcoming features (`Kanban`, `Contacts`, `Snoozed`, `Rules`, `AI`, `Translation`, `Cloud Sync`) inside the unified Harbor surface language with honest disabled states and clear unavailability notes.
donts: Don't add thick (`3px`–`4px`) colored side-stripes to mail rows, privacy banners, callouts, or active navigation items; use `1px` hairlines, leading `6px` pips, or inset focus-isolation borders instead.
Don't place uppercase eyebrow kickers above pane titles, settings headers, or dialog headings, and never apply `text-transform: uppercase` to bilingual Chinese/English navigation section labels.
Don't reintroduce multiple competing application-shell themes; keep `harbor` as the single application visual system with independent `light` / `dark` / `system` color modes.
Don't load external web fonts, icon CDNs, or third-party stylesheets at runtime.
Don't paint unread mail rows with a competing background fill that fights selected-row focus isolation, or reuse Terracotta signal hues for decorative accents.
Don't add decorative staggered entrance animations to workspace lists, tabs, or dialogs; keep motion strictly to `150ms`–`190ms` state transitions.
Don't hardcode raw `#ffffff` button text against `var(--color-accent)` without using `var(--color-accent-contrast)` (`#08131d` in dark mode), or dark-mode primary buttons lose text contrast.
